subject: 🏃 Sunday — 6 mi Recovery Run (Wk 4)
html:
Tomorrow: 6 mi recovery run, 9:30+/mi, HR cap ≤145. This is the day after a 10K race you ran through a cold — the body is paying down two debts (race effort + viral load), and the only job is gentle blood flow. No pace targets, no progression, no testing the legs. If pace drifts to 10:00, great. Flat route preferred — Bayfront paths if you're up for it, neighborhood loop if not.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction), banded lateral walks (10 each), glute bridges (10 reps, 2-sec hold), quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 each side). Keep it light — this is a wake-up, not a warm-up for intensity.

Illness check before you lace up: If the cold has worsened overnight — chest involvement, new fever, RHR elevated >5 bpm over baseline, or energy noticeably worse than Saturday — skip the run entirely and take a rest day or do 30 min easy bike at HR <120. A recovery run only helps if the immune system isn't still fighting hard. The long run is shifted to next Sunday (12 mi, Jun 7) regardless, so there's zero training cost to resting today.

Knee veto: 2+ on waking → 30 min easy bike instead. Yesterday's 10K was 46 min of sustained Z4 effort, and the knee was 1/5 at the finish — strong signal — but respect any morning-after awareness.

Focus cue: Wear the H10. Yesterday's race data was clean because the strap was on — keep that habit locked in for every run, including easy days. The recovery-run HR trace is actually useful coaching data (resting cardiac cost of easy movement post-race + post-illness).

Context: This closes Phase 1, Week 4 of 12 — 56 days to the SF Marathon. Four weeks of foundation work banked with knee 1/5 across every session. Yesterday's 7:17/mi while sick is a fitness floor, not a ceiling — Tuesday's 6×1000m at 6:54 avg remains the clean VDOT 54–55 calibration. Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold) starts tomorrow with the Boston trip: Monday hip circuit at home before the 10 AM flight, then Esplanade tempo work Tue/Thu. Hydrate well today, keep zinc + Vit C going, and get to bed early — the eastbound jet lag hits hardest Tue/Wed and you want to bank sleep before Monday's travel day.
